messages.subject: some questions about unrooted tree
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I have some questions about unrooted tree. My code is as follows.

treeg <- read.tree("genome_fasttree.txt")
groupg <- read.table("genome_tree_annotation.txt",header=T,sep="\t")
groupginfo_g <-split(groupg$strain,groupg$species)

treegg<-ggtree(treeg,layout="daylight",size=3,branch.length='none')
treegg_group<-groupOTU(treegg,groupginfo_g,'host')+aes(color=host)+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#1a1a1a","#f46d43","#3288bd","#1a9850","#c51b7d"))+
  geom_tiplab(size=8)+
  theme(legend.position="right")

pg<-treegg_group+new_scale_fill()
pg1<-pg+new_scale_color()
cluster<-groupg[,c(2,3)]

pg2<-pg1 %<+% cluster +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color=cluster,shape=cluster),alpha=.7,shape=16)+
  scale_color_manual(breaks=c("Gillia_Acer_1","Gillia_Acer_2","Gillia_Acer_3","Gillia_Acer_4","Gillia_Acer_5","none"),values=c("#66c2a5","#8da0cb","#e78ac3","#a6d854","#ffd92f","#737373"))+
  scale_shape_manual(breaks=c("Gillia_Acer_1","Gillia_Acer_2","Gillia_Acer_3","Gillia_Acer_4","Gillia_Acer_5","NA"),values=c(21,22,23,24,25,21))
pg2
ggsave("genome_tree2.pdf",treegg_group,width=48,height=40)

I have two problems.
First, my tip label embedded in the branches as the picture.
Second, the error information as follows:
> pg2
错误: Insufficient values in manual scale. 11 needed but only 6 provided.

I don't know how to solve the problems. Thank you for your help.

messages.subject: How to collapse by species and annotating data onto collapsed tree?
messages.subject_clean: How to collapse by species and annotating data onto collapsed tree?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Yu,

I am dealing with the problem of adding numerical attributes to parents nodes. As the picture shows, the phylogeny was built with individuals, while several individuals constitute a species(1-7). Some of the species are monophyletic while some are not. I would like to map the genetic diversity level for every species on to the tree, but find it's hard to find solution to the following problems:
1. How to collapse by species?
I tried to collapse every node using collapse(p, node = 100) but it requires a line of code for each node, which I found inefficient and foolish.
2. How to add label to collapsed node?
I would like to add species name to this collapsed node, but "clade_name = 'species'" didn't do the job.
3. How to add numerical attributes to every collapsed node? (as green bars with numbers in the attached picture)

My best,
Wu

messages.subject: gheatmap - how to remove cell border entirely
messages.subject_clean: gheatmap - how to remove cell border entirely
messages.body_plain:
I'd like to entirely remove the cell border from the phylogenetic heat map because when visualizing 1000's of species, the cells become over-shadowed by the border and less discernible, as shown in this figure:

>From the documentation of gheatmap, I see that there is an argument called "color", which changes the color of the cell border. However, I would like to remove it entirely. For example, it would be great if I could simply specify something like: gheatmap(color = "blank")

I've been modifying the code from the vignette to create my figure:

nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="treeio")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
circ <- ggtree(tree, layout = "circular")
df <- data.frame(first=c("a", "b", "a", "c", "d", "d", "a", "b", "e", "e", "f", "c", "f"),
                 second= c("z", "z", "z", "z", "y", "y", "y", "y", "x", "x", "x", "a", "a"))
rownames(df) <- tree$tip.label
df2 <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(39), ncol=3))
rownames(df2) <- tree$tip.label
colnames(df2) <- LETTERS[1:3]
p1 <- gheatmap(circ, df, offset=.8, width=.2,
               colnames_angle=95, colnames_offset_y = .25) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option="D", name="discrete\nvalue")
library(ggnewscale)
p2 <- p1 + new_scale_fill()
gheatmap(p2, df2, offset=15, width=.3,
         colnames_angle=90, colnames_offset_y = .25) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="A", name="continuous\nvalue")

My goal is to visualize life-history traits in this huge phylogeny with colors. The gheatmap() function seems like a great way to go, however if there are alternative methods for acquiring a similar effect, I am open to suggestions.

Thanks for this wonderful package!
